rationale: C06 plausibly supplied a material proclamation template: recitals identify a social need, organized public and private efforts, and congressional authorization for a designated month; the operative text then sets apart that month and urges named professions, media, agencies, and individuals to unite in an intensive campaign. The child follows the same sequence for Korean relief, adapting the designated period, beneficiary, sponsoring organization, and requested contributions. C09 and C12 contain nearly the same machinery but are earlier and slightly less textually close.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Congress of the United States by joint Resolution ... has authorized the President to set aside a period of time for intensive effort
shared_material.parent_excerpt: by Public Resolution 82 ... the President is authorized and requested to issue annually a proclamation setting apart the month of April of each year as Cancer Control Month
shared_material.explanation: Both use congressional authorization as the final predicate for proclaiming a special period devoted to a public campaign.

shared_material.child_excerpt: do hereby set aside and proclaim the month of September, 1951, as a special period of intensive effort
shared_material.parent_excerpt: do hereby set apart the month of April 1950 as Cancer Control Month
shared_material.explanation: The central operative act uses closely parallel language to designate an entire month for the campaign.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I call upon our citizens, our schools, our churches, and all our civic and patriotic organizations to respond promptly and bountifully
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I also urge the medical profession, the press, the radio and motion-picture industries, and all interested agencies and individuals to unite during April 1950
shared_material.explanation: Both follow the monthly designation with an appeal to an enumerated set of public institutions, organizations, and individuals to support the campaign during that month.
